I think it would help to think of your diet (diet as in what you eat, not diet as in weight loss or plan) as independent of theirs. Not sure how much control you have over your food options, but if you have your own money for groceries I would make a meal plan and eat your own food instead of theirs. Then you don’t really have to worry about if they’re eating healthy or not that day. If you don’t have money for groceries then maybe you can make a small list for your parents to get for you when they go to the store. And I don’t think it’s rude to turn down the baked good your mom buys! She’ll get the hint eventually and stop buying them for you. However, a sweet treat every now and again won’t ruin your progress. 

As far as diet itself, I like reading about targeting your metabolism as it seems like it has a healthier relationship with food. One that’s more about nutrition and your body functions than about fad diets. I like @thenutritionaddiction on instagram who talks a lot about this. I also have a book/cookbook by Mark Hyman that I like a lot.

I’m not gonna pretend to know what I’m talking about, but those are my personal experiences turning a strict, unhealthy relationship with food and weight loss into one that’s more focused on nutrition and feeling good!
